skill.name: amazon-competitor-analyzer
skill.description: Scrapes Amazon product data from ASINs using browseract.com automation API and performs surgical competitive analysis. Compares specifications, pricing, review quality, and visual strategies to identify competitor moats and vulnerabilities.
skill.summary: Collects Amazon product data through BrowserAct and compares pricing, ratings, and review volume across ASINs.
skill.author: browser-act

security_audit.summary: Most high-severity detections are false positives from placeholders, expected credential handling, Markdown fences, and documented environment setup. The executable makes disclosed BrowserAct requests and writes reports to user-selected directories. CLI secrets and unescaped spreadsheet fields remain meaningful risks.

remediation.issue: API keys can be supplied through a command-line option.
remediation.suggestion: Remove or deprecate --api-key. Read the key from the environment or a secure interactive prompt.

remediation.issue: External product fields can become active spreadsheet formulas.
remediation.suggestion: Neutralize CSV cells beginning with equals, plus, minus, or at signs before writing them.

remediation.issue: The setup guidance does not protect the credential-bearing .env file.
remediation.suggestion: Add .env to source-control exclusions and document restrictive file permissions and key rotation.

remediation.issue: Report generation overwrites predictable filenames without confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Refuse existing destinations by default or require an explicit overwrite option.

remediation.issue: Dotenv loading imports every entry from the local file.
remediation.suggestion: Parse only BROWSERACT_API_KEY or document that all local .env values enter the process environment.

semantic_findings.title: API Key Exposed Through Command Arguments
semantic_findings.description: The --api-key option places a credential in command arguments, which may persist in shell history and appear in process listings.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The argparse option directly accepts the API key as a command-line value, a well-established local credential exposure path.

semantic_findings.title: Spreadsheet Formula Injection in CSV Reports
semantic_findings.description: Externally sourced product fields are written to CSV without neutralizing formula prefixes, which can trigger formulas when a report opens.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Product title, brand, and feature values flow from the API response into csv.writer without checks for equals, plus, minus, or at signs.

semantic_findings.title: Incomplete Secret Storage Guidance
semantic_findings.description: Setup directs users to store a real key in .env without warning them to exclude that file from version control.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both files explicitly direct creation of a credential-bearing .env file, while the reviewed setup text provides no source-control warning.

content.value_statement: Manual Amazon competitor research is slow and inconsistent. This skill retrieves product data through BrowserAct, compares core metrics, and creates local reports.
actual_capabilities: Validates one or more 10-character alphanumeric ASINs before submission.
Submits BrowserAct workflow tasks and polls until each task finishes, fails, or times out.
Retrieves product results and compares price ranges, ratings, and review volume.
Exports product data as CSV, Markdown, and JSON files.
Accepts a BrowserAct API key from the environment, constructor, or command-line option.
limitations: Requires a BrowserAct account, API key, internet access, and an available external workflow.
Depends on a fixed workflow template and the response fields returned by BrowserAct.
Does not implement claimed sentiment, visual, moat, vulnerability, or detailed specification analysis.
Always writes CSV, Markdown, and JSON reports because the documented format option is not implemented.

use_cases.title: Compare a Product Shortlist
use_cases.description: Collect prices, ratings, and review counts for candidate products before prioritizing deeper research.

use_cases.title: Benchmark Market Pricing
use_cases.description: Compare the lowest and highest observed prices across selected ASINs and export the source data.

use_cases.title: Track Competing Listings
use_cases.description: Create repeatable local reports for a known set of competing Amazon listings.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze One ASIN

prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner analysis of one known product

prompt_templates.title: Compare Several Products
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these ASINs: [ASIN_LIST]. Summarize price, rating, and review volume differences, then save the reports to [OUTPUT_DIRECTORY].
prompt_templates.scenario: Basic comparison of a product shortlist

prompt_templates.title: Benchmark Pricing and Reviews
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [ASIN_LIST]. Identify the lowest price, highest price, top rating, and largest review volume using only retrieved data.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Competitive Dataset
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [ASIN_LIST] and save reports to [OUTPUT_DIRECTORY]. Flag failed records, missing fields, and metric outliers without inventing unavailable insights.

output_examples.input: Analyze one valid ASIN and save results to the current directory.
output_examples.output: The skill validates the ASIN, retrieves its BrowserAct result, and creates CSV, Markdown, and JSON report files.

output_examples.input: Compare four competing ASINs for pricing and ratings.
output: Price positioning identifies the observed lowest and highest prices.
Rating analysis identifies the highest rating and orders products by review volume.
Failed or unavailable product records remain visible in the generated reports.

output_examples.output: The skill reports the invalid identifier and skips submission for that item.

best_practices: Use only ASINs that you are authorized to research and follow applicable marketplace terms.
Store the BrowserAct key in a protected environment variable and review report destinations before running.
Verify missing fields and failed tasks before using the comparison for business decisions.
anti_patterns: Do not pass production API keys through shared shell commands or recorded automation logs.
Do not treat the output as sentiment, visual, or moat analysis because those features are not implemented.
Do not overwrite an existing report directory without reviewing its current files.

faq.question: What credentials are required?
faq.answer: A BrowserAct API key is required. The skill reads BROWSERACT_API_KEY or accepts a key through its Python interface.

faq.question: Does the skill access Amazon directly?
faq.answer: No. It submits ASINs to a fixed BrowserAct workflow and retrieves the resulting task data.

faq.question: Which report formats are generated?
faq.answer: The implementation generates CSV, Markdown, and JSON reports together.

faq.question: What comparisons are implemented?
faq.answer: It compares observed prices, average ratings, and review counts. Other advertised strategy analysis is not implemented.

faq.question: How are invalid ASINs handled?
faq.answer: Each ASIN must contain exactly ten alphanumeric characters. Invalid values are reported and skipped.

faq.question: Can reports replace existing files?
faq.answer: Yes. The current implementation writes predictable filenames and can replace existing reports in the selected directory.
